dedupe_keys.name: galileo navigation and timing service outage july 2019

description: This post-event case covers the six-day interruption of the Galileo initial navigation and timing services from 10 to 17 July 2019, the longest outage of any global navigation satellite system in service. During an upgrade of the ground segment, when the usual redundancy between the two Galileo control centres was temporarily unavailable, temporary equipment installed for the upgrade was mishandled; the time and orbit determination function failed and correct navigation messages could no longer be generated, so the satellites broadcast stale data and users were told not to use the signals. The European Commission set up an Independent Inquiry Board of Member State experts in transport, space and defence projects, which delivered final recommendations on 4 November 2019 on governance, operations and redundancy, and the Galileo quarterly performance report for the third quarter documented the service loss and recovery. Coverage: the worldwide Galileo service and its European ground segment, July 2019. Format and access: free Commission press release, performance report and news analyses; the full Inquiry Board report was not published. Caveats: the public account is a summary; impacts on users were limited because most receivers combine Galileo with GPS, so the case shows ground-segment fragility more than user losses. Simulation uses: a reference for cascading failure inside a satellite system through its ground control, recovery and restoration timelines of navigation services, and resilience testing of multi-constellation dependence. Related records: the Galileo quarterly performance reports give service statistics, and the GPS UTC offset anomaly of January 2016 is a comparable ground-segment event.
